source: Census 2011 KS201/DC2101 + Census 2021 TS021/RM032 (NOMIS) + ONS SNPP 2022-based Z1
methodology: Hamilton-Perry v7.0 single-year-of-age model with 20 ethnic groups. Census 2021 base from ONS custom dataset (direct observations, no IPF). Census 2011 base from DC2101EW (18 groups, 21 age bands, Beers interpolation to single-year; Roma split from Gypsy/Traveller using 2021 proportions). 91 age groups x 20 ethnic groups x 2 sexes. SNPP 2022-based envelope constraint (linear extrapolation beyond 2047). Brexit WHO adjustment (-15% growth ages 20-44). DfE School Census 2024/25 calibration (20% damped CCR adjustment for ages 0-5). Backcast validated: MAE 1.71pp across 269 areas (beats NEWETHPOP 2.58pp by 33%). Monte Carlo stochastic: 1000 simulations, sigma=0.02.

knownLimitations.description: 4% of people change their ethnic self-identification between censuses (Simpson, Jivraj & Warren 2016, ONS Longitudinal Study). This rate is doubling each decade. For Mixed categories, 43% reclassify. CCRs capture reclassification as if it were demographic change.
knownLimitations.status: Cannot fix until ONS publishes 2011-2021 LS reclassification data (expected 2025-2026). Mixed category projections carry additional uncertainty.
knownLimitations.reference: Simpson, L., Jivraj, S. & Warren, J. (2016) 'The stability of ethnic group and religion in the Censuses of England and Wales 2001-2011'. Demographic Research.

knownLimitations.description: CCRs conflate ethnic population dynamics with deprivation-driven selective migration. Areas undergoing regeneration will see different ethnic trajectories than the CCR predicts.
knownLimitations.status: Requires IMD stratification. Future work: compute separate CCRs by deprivation quintile.

knownLimitations.description: 693K people emigrated from the UK in YE June 2025. ONS does not publish emigration by ethnic group, only by nationality. Model uses net migration implicitly via CCRs but cannot distinguish immigration from emigration dynamics.
knownLimitations.status: No fix possible without ethnic emigration data. CCRs capture net effect only.

knownLimitations.description: ONS linked births data (from 2007) could provide direct ethnic-specific Age-Specific Fertility Rates. The US Census Bureau uses race-specific ASFRs. This would be more accurate than CCR-implied fertility.
knownLimitations.status: Data exists but requires formal ONS data request. Future improvement.
knownLimitations.reference: ONS Birth Characteristics linked dataset; US Census Bureau 2023 projections methodology

knownLimitations.description: Census 2021 taken during third COVID lockdown (21 March 2021). Internal migration patterns disrupted. International students absent from term-time addresses. University-heavy LAs flagged with widened confidence intervals.
knownLimitations.status: Partially mitigated: student-heavy LAs flagged (covidCaveat=true). Cannot fully correct without non-COVID reference data.
knownLimitations.reference: ONS Census 2021 General Report, Chapter on COVID-19 adjustments
